01 · THE CHALLENGE

Defaults are visible. Can we spot risk earlier?

Start with the full portfolio baseline.

Business question: Which borrower and loan details help FinNova identify higher-risk loans early, without automatically excluding borrowers who could repay?
02 · PORTFOLIO CONTEXT

What kind of loans are in the portfolio?

Loan purpose provides context. It is not among the strongest seven standalone indicators, so this is a compact summary—not a full-page chart.

03 · REPAYMENT CAPACITY

Can borrowers comfortably afford the loan?

DTI, LTI and monthly EMI are the strongest standalone indicators in the training-sample AUC screening.

Debt-to-income ratio (DTI)

Monthly debt payments compared with monthly income.

Select a bar for the exact count and default rate.
DTI = (monthly EMI + existing monthly debt) ÷ monthly income. Higher DTI means more income is already committed to debt payments.

Loan-to-income ratio (LTI)

Loan amount compared with annual income.

Select a bar for the exact count and default rate.
LTI = loan amount ÷ annual income. It shows how large the loan is relative to the borrower's yearly income.

Monthly EMI

Select a bar for the exact count and default rate.

05 · INFORMATION AVAILABILITY

A missing field is not automatically a risky borrower.

Credit score can be missing because the borrower was unscored. Utilisation can be missing because no revolving credit line was reported.

Missing information groups

How we handle it

For this prototype, missing numeric values are filled with the training-sample median. Missingness itself does not add a risk penalty.

This avoids treating “not available” as “bad”.

06 · EXISTING GRADES

The current A–E grades identify some risk—but leave room to improve.

We assess the grades as supplied. The workbook does not disclose the formula used to assign them.

07 · SELECTING THE INPUTS

Which indicators are strongest on their own?

We tested all eligible numeric inputs using AUC on the training sample. These are the seven highest risk-oriented AUC values.

Top seven · training AUC

What does AUC mean?

AUC checks how often a randomly selected defaulter receives a higher risk reading than a randomly selected non-defaulter, after adjusting the direction of the indicator.

0.50 is chance-level separation. Higher values mean stronger standalone separation.

AUC selects useful inputs. It does not, by itself, calculate the combined model weights.

Weights estimated by logistic regression

The model uses signed coefficients to calculate risk. “Relative weight” is the absolute share of coefficient sizes for communication only; it is not a standalone percentage probability. Some coefficients become small or change direction when related measures are considered together; this is a warning that DTI, LTI, EMI and loan amount overlap and the scorecard needs further refinement.

08 · PROPOSED A–E GRADES

The new grades use combined predicted risk.

A logistic regression combines the seven indicators and estimates a default probability for each loan.

Grade bands and probability cut-offs

How it works: each input is standardised using training data, multiplied by its fitted coefficient, and combined. The model converts that total into a predicted default probability. The grade bands are set using training-sample probability cut-offs.
09 · DOES IT IMPROVE DEFAULT IDENTIFICATION?

The proposed model catches more defaults at a similar review volume.

Both systems are compared on the same untouched holdout sample.

Default rate within each grade

Business implication

D/E is a priority-review group for this comparison, not an automatic rejection rule.

Recommendation for E-grade borrowers: Do not automatically reject everyone. In the holdout sample, 411 of 924 E-grade loans defaulted (44.5%); 513 (55.5%) were not marked as defaults. Use enhanced verification and manual review first. The business must weigh missed defaults against good borrowers turned away.
Aspirational next step: A human-supervised AI agent could assemble evidence, run checks, explain risk flags and route cases for review. Final lending decisions should remain with authorised staff until thoroughly validated.
